title: The lane that Partition never left
excerpt: A narrow street in Old Delhi where the old families still live. They never talk about 1947. But everything they do is shaped by it.
body:
Gali Qasim Jan is quiet in the afternoons. The families that came in 1947 are harder to find in the records, because no one wrote down what happened in the weeks of partition the way historians prefer things to be written.

Mrs Krishnamurthy, 84, came from Lahore as a six-year-old. She does not speak about it directly. But when she shows me her kitchen, she points to the recipes she still makes from her mother's memory — recipes with ingredients that were common in Lahore and rare in Delhi. "The taste is not quite right," she says. "It was never quite right again."
